routes.label: Count by the attributes that change

question: A child has a set of \(96\) distinct blocks. Each block is one of \(2\) materials (plastic, wood), \(3\) sizes (small, medium, large), \(4\) colors (blue, green, red, yellow), and \(4\) shapes (circle, hexagon, square, triangle). How many blocks in the set are different from the “plastic medium red circle” in exactly two ways? (The “wood medium red square” is such a block.)
solution:
There are \(2\cdot3\cdot4\cdot4=96\) possible material, size, color, and shape combinations, so the set contains one block of each combination.

Relative to the plastic medium red circle, a changed material has \(1\) choice, a changed size has \(2\) choices, a changed color has \(3\) choices, and a changed shape has \(3\) choices. An unchanged attribute has just its original value.

Classify the desired blocks by which two attributes change. The six possible pairs are material and size, material and color, material and shape, size and color, size and shape, and color and shape. For each pair, multiply the numbers of alternative values. If \(N\) is the desired count, then
\[
\begin{aligned}
N&=1\cdot2+1\cdot3+1\cdot3\\
&\quad+2\cdot3+2\cdot3+3\cdot3\\
&=2+3+3+6+6+9=29.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every eligible block changes one of these six pairs, and its pair of changed attributes is unique, so no block is omitted or counted twice. The answer is \(\boxed{29}\), choice A.
